registered_before: any leave-one-out model is fitted or scored
owner_decision: 30/10, supervisor's request: the ablation must drop every pair and every feature of base29 and evaluate all of them, not only four chosen pairs
question: Which of the 29 tracked syscalls (alone) and which functional pairs carry detection signal in Pulse, measured as the loss in recall and in attack-minus-benign separation when only that syscall's explicit channels are removed?

arms.drop_<syscall>: 29 arms: one tracked syscall's explicit channels removed (log-count, ratio, rolling mean, rolling std: 4 of 249 columns per context window)
arms.pairs: 7 arms: accept/accept4, open/openat, execve/execveat, clone/clone3 (the 4 pairs of the earlier study, refitted here), sendto/recvfrom, recvmmsg/sendmmsg, setuid/setgid
arms.what_stays: the dropped syscall still contributes to the 64 hashed syscall bins, the 64 syscall-pair bins and the 5 aggregates (sensitive-syscall share included); the ablation measures the explicit channel, not every trace of the syscall. Removing it from the pair bins is impossible from stored counts (pair order is not stored); this is reported as a limitation

data_and_fit: exactly the syscall-arms study inputs (pulse-soak-baseline selection capture, matched-parallel-r4-20261015, sealed feature segments and attack-interval exclusions) and its fit settings (sentinel_pulse/syscall_study/matched_study.py with arm_set=loo: ExtraTrees 192 trees + support branch, train cap 3000, calibration cap 1500, same context indices for every arm), 21 workloads

stages.stage_1_screening: every arm with one seed (73021): 37 x 21 = 777 models
stages.stage_2_confirmation: seeds 73021-73023 for base29, every arm whose stage-1 recall or separation difference to base29 has a 95 % CI excluding 0 or a point estimate beyond +-2 points, and the 11 sensitive syscalls regardless (mprotect, chmod, ptrace, setuid, setgid, capset, pivot_root, mount, unshare, setns, seccomp, plus execve and execveat)
stages.conclusions: only from stage 2; stage-1-only arms are reported as screening

evaluation: the syscall study's chain unchanged: matched normal holdout with recalibration as Pulse (matched_holdout.py), budget matching under k2of2 (arm_budget.py) at 1 and 5 episodes per replica-hour, attack replay on pulse-attack-dev and on pulse-live-recalibrated (the campaign with benign-binary controls) (arm_attack_replay.py), paired workload-clustered bootstrap 95 % CIs vs base29 (arm_bootstrap.py, 10,000 draws)
metrics: recall, benign-binary flag rate and separation (recall - benign rate), control rate, p95 latency, per scenario and pooled, at matched budget

criteria.needed: an arm whose recall or separation difference to base29 is below 0 with the upper 95 % CI bound < 0 after Holm correction over the stage-2 arms
criteria.removable: recall and separation differences with 95 % CI lower bounds >= -2 points AND p95 not slower by more than 0.2 s at both budgets
criteria.no_change_to_pulse: no feature-set change follows from this study alone; a removable set would need its own registered live confirmation

known_dependence: these are development data: the same captures selected base29 and the earlier arms; the 5 attack scenarios are exposed (as in the syscall study). LID-DS 2021 can be used as an external check of any removable set
schedule: after pulse-live-recal-confirm, its analysis and the queued LID-DS/CB-DS jobs on .234 (MemoryMax 32 GB, no live run active)
code: sentinel_pulse/syscall_study/matched_study.py (arm_set=loo, seeds configurable; tests/test_matched_study.py) and the unchanged evaluation scripts
